title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
annotation: Introduces keyed green-list logit bias and an interpretable statistical detector. Treated as the PRIMARY candidate mechanism for hypothesis testing against Claude-generated text (docs/research/CLAUDE_WATERMARK_HYPOTHESIS.md); no public evidence establishes Anthropic deploys it. PMLR v202 pp.17061-17084; arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2301.10226. Section 7 self-attack (span replacement under rising budget) is the methodological precedent for constrained perturbation analysis.
implementation_use: canonical generator; canonical detector; positive control; Claude hypothesis model; perturbation baseline; hybridization anchor; parameter-search target; robustness benchmark

title: On the Reliability of Watermarks for Large Language Models
annotation: Extends the reliability analysis of the KGW family and examines practical attacks and statistical behavior. It supplies critical conditions for calibration and stress testing.

title: Robust Distortion-Free Watermarks for Language Models
annotation: Develops a distortion-free construction based on alignment with a secret random sequence. Results show that detectability depends strongly on output entropy and task.

title: Unbiased Watermark for Large Language Models
annotation: Proposes a watermark that preserves the model's marginal distribution under stated assumptions. The paper is required background for testing any claim that a method is unbiased.

title: Scalable Watermarking for Identifying Large Language Model Outputs
annotation: Describes scalable tournament-sampling watermarking and deployment-oriented evaluation. It is useful for system design even though outside researchers cannot reproduce proprietary deployment details.

title: Undetectable Watermarks for Language Models
annotation: Develops cryptographic constructions intended to be computationally indistinguishable without the secret key. It clarifies the difference between public stylistic detection and keyed verification.

title: Provable Robust Watermarking for AI-Generated Text
annotation: Provides robustness guarantees under a formal text-editing model. The formal assumptions should be compared with actual academic editing and translation workflows before operational use.

title: Can Watermarks Survive Translation?
annotation: Shows that pivot-language translation can reduce tested watermark discrimination toward chance and proposes X-SIR. This is essential for a multilingual threat model.

title: Bypassing LLM Watermarks with Color-Aware Substitutions
annotation: Demonstrates black-box inference of token-color structure followed by targeted substitutions. It motivates query controls, key rotation, and adaptive attack tests.
implementation_use: color-aware attack plugin; API rate-limit tests

title: Paraphrasing Evades Detectors of AI-Generated Text
annotation: Shows that paraphrasing evades several AI-text detectors while retrieval may help in some provenance settings. It is broader than watermarking but important for adversarial evaluation.

title: No Free Lunch in LLM Watermarking
annotation: Formalizes trade-offs among watermark robustness, utility, and usability. It prevents the project from treating a single high detection score as proof of general superiority.

title: Watermarks in the Sand
annotation: Provides impossibility results for strong watermarking guarantees in broad settings. It supports a layered provenance strategy rather than watermark-only governance.

title: RAID: A Shared Benchmark for Robust Evaluation of Machine-Generated Text Detectors
annotation: Benchmarks detectors across a large and diverse collection of generations and attacks. It is a model for stratified evaluation and for avoiding single-dataset accuracy claims.

title: A Survey of Text Watermarking in the Era of Large Language Models
annotation: Synthesizes watermark types, requirements, attacks, and evaluation practices. It is useful for terminology and coverage audits, but implementation claims should return to primary method papers.

title: Mark My Words: Analyzing and Evaluating Language Model Watermarks
annotation: Benchmarks quality, token requirement, and tamper resistance. It highlights task dependence and the greater difficulty of watermarking code.
implementation_use: benchmark protocol; length bins; code tests

title: SoK: Watermarking for AI-Generated Content
annotation: Systematizes properties, threat models, evaluation criteria, and open problems across modalities. Nicholas Carlini is listed with an Anthropic affiliation, making this the clearest verified core research connection.
implementation_use: threat model; evaluation framework; Anthropic audit

title: Improved Unbiased Watermark for Large Language Models
annotation: Introduces a multi-channel method with stronger reported detection than prior unbiased approaches. Robustness varies sharply by attack, so the adapter must reproduce each condition rather than quote one headline value.

title: MirrorMark: Generalizable Mirrored Sampling for Multi-bit LLM Watermarking
annotation: Uses mirrored pseudorandom mappings and context-anchored scheduling for multi-bit watermarking. Current results distinguish detection from payload recovery, and the paper has no verified Anthropic connection.

title: GPT Detectors Are Biased Against Non-Native English Writers
annotation: Finds substantial false-positive risk for non-native English writing in generic detectors. It justifies language and author-group calibration and a prohibition on automatic accusations.

title: Can AI-Generated Text Be Reliably Detected?
annotation: Argues theoretically and empirically that generic detection degrades under distribution shift and paraphrasing. It supports the separation between keyed verification and style classification.
